newsitem.title: UK: Lloyd's says issues writs to 200 Canadian Names.
newsitem.headline: Lloyd's says issues writs to 200 Canadian Names.

text.p: Lloyd's of London said on Friday it has issued writs to nearly 200 investors in Canada, seeking to recover around 80 million stg in debts owed by them.

A spokesman for the insurance market said 343 writs were issued through the High Court to 197 Names, as the investors are called, who did not accept its 3.2 billion stg settlement offer compensating them for 8.0 billion stg losses from 1988 to 1992.

The settlement offer was declared unconditional in September after more than 90 percent of Names accepted. Under the terms of the offer, the Names helped pay to reinsure those losses into a new company called Equitas.

This brings to 322 the number of Names who have been sent writs. Lloyd's started legal action earlier this month against 125 UK Names. There are 1,800 or so worldwide who did not accept the offer and who owe an estimated 500 million stg.
Earlier this week, the insurance market sent out almost 320 warning letters to Names in the United States telling them they had 14 days in which to accept or writs would follow.

In addition, around 450 investors faced possible court action if they did not withdraw by the end of today "conditions" they imposed that the market has refused to grant. Lloyd's was unable to say on Friday afternoon how many had done this.
